tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...', 'Use it for...'), focuses on user intent (slow storage, alarms firing, sizing questions, stuck modifications, snapshot review, KMS errors, bill jumps, pre-launch review) rather than internals, is pushy by explicitly listing many trigger contexts and metric names even when the user doesn't name EBS directly, and ends with an explicit negative scope statement. It is a dense paragraph but stays within a reasonable length for the breadth of triggers it must cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user wants to know why Amazon EBS storage is slow, why an EBS alarm fired, or whether their EBS setup is production-ready, even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower or ask whether to add IOPS.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what EBS is, what IOPS means) and instead focuses on domain-specific procedures, non-obvious facts, and workflow steps the agent wouldn't know without this skill.
tests.evidence: 'A modification in `optimizing` is not stuck. The new size, IOPS or throughput already applies while it optimizes.' — this is specific, non-obvious domain knowledge, not general explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps detailed reference data (metric thresholds, API lists, error tables) in dedicated reference files and only summarizes high-level workflow and rules inline; the classification table links to path-specific files rather than embedding their content.
tests.evidence: 'Load [references/metrics-thresholds.md](references/metrics-thresholds.md) for any metric judgement.' shows thresholds are deferred to a reference file rather than embedded.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via a markdown link somewhere in the body (data-collection, ebs-best-practices, finding-logic, metrics-thresholds, review-operational, review-report-format, troubleshoot-billing, troubleshoot-encryption, troubleshoot-performance, troubleshoot-snapshots, troubleshoot-volume-modification).
tests.evidence: '[references/troubleshoot-performance.md](references/troubleshoot-performance.md): performance attribution, the live-tested procedure' and similar links for all other files in the References section.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a specific triggering condition or purpose describing when to load it, e.g., tied to user phrasing/alarm patterns in the classification table or to specific judgement needs in Step 2.
tests.evidence: '"My app is slow", high latency, an alarm on AWS/EBS metrics ... | Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md](references/troubleshoot-performance.md) |' specifies exactly when to load the file.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references to files use relative paths from the skill root in the format references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (verdict format, change proposals, approval flow) are prescribed exactly, while flexible areas (e.g., choosing which path fits ambiguous requests) are given reasoning and freedom ('If a request fits more than one row, answer the question the user asked first').
tests.evidence: 'A typed "approve" in chat is not approval, and the reply says so in those words whenever the user types an approval.' shows exact prescription for a fragile approval-safety operation, appropriately strict.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple equal tool/approach options for the same task without guidance; it routes to a single applicable reference per scenario via the classification table, which functions as a clear default-selection mechanism rather than a menu of equal choices.
tests.evidence: The classification table maps each symptom type to exactly one path/reference, e.g. 'Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md]' — no competing equal options listed.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classify-then-investigate-then-validate procedure applicable to any EBS troubleshooting/review request, not a one-off instance; specific details like formats and rules are embedded within this generalizable approach.
tests.evidence: 'Follow the numbered procedure in the loaded path. Discover every value from the APIs... Then draft the report in the format below.' describes a reusable approach, not a one-shot declaration.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated Gotchas section with concrete, specific, non-obvious corrections relevant to the EBS domain.
tests.evidence: '`DescribeInstanceTypes` reports EBS bandwidth in MB/s. Convert it to MiB/s before comparing it with volume throughput.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly defines output templates/formats for both modes (troubleshoot verdict format, review Summary table format) and defers detailed layout to review-report-format.md, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.
tests.evidence: 'Review mode uses the rated report in [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md). Every Review mode response MUST begin with its Summary table...' shows a template is provided/referenced.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The inline 'Troubleshoot verdict format' template is short (6 bullet items, well under 20 lines) and the longer Review mode report format is deferred to a separate reference file (review-report-format.md) rather than embedded in the body.
tests.evidence: The troubleshoot verdict format list (Answer, Evidence, Binding layer, Recommendation, Separate findings, Gaps) is only 6 short lines; the longer review format is offloaded to 'references/review-report-format.md'.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The skill presents its main workflow as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N' labels, and the detailed sections below use matching '## Step N:' headings that reference the same step numbers.
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Classify the request' ... followed by '## Step 1: Classify the Request', '## Step 2: Load the Shared References', '## Step 3: Run the Path and Draft the Report', '## Step 4: Check the Draft Before Presenting It' — matching step numbers throughout.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation step (Step 4) instructing the agent to check its draft output against multiple correctness criteria before presenting it to the user.
tests.evidence: '## Step 4: Check the Draft Before Presenting It\n\nReview the draft from Step 3 against these checks. Fix anything that fails, then present it.' followed by criteria like 'Every number under Evidence came from an API call made in this session, has its unit and time window...'
